name: Georgia

rates2026.note: state law (O.C.G.A. 34-4-3) sets $5.15, below the federal rate; the federal $7.25 applies to nearly all workers

tipped.note: federal tipped cash wage; Georgia's state minimum wage law does not apply to tipped employees

minWage.other: Georgia's own minimum wage is $5.15/hour (O.C.G.A. 34-4-3), but with limited exceptions the federal $7.25 applies.

source.quote: Georgia's minimum wage is $5.15 per hour, however, with some limited exceptions, the federal minimum wage rate applies.

tippedSource.quote: An employer of a tipped employee is only required to pay $2.13 an hour in direct wages, if that amount plus the tips received equals at least the federal minimum wage

overtime.exemptSalaryNote: no state salary threshold; federal FLSA rules apply
overtime.note: No state overtime law; the federal FLSA (time and a half after 40 hours a week) applies.

source.quote: Unless specifically exempted, employees must receive overtime pay for hours worked in excess of 40 in a workweek at a rate of 1 and 1/2 their regular rates of pay.
Neither federal nor state law requires that an employer provide vacation, sick, or personal leave.
Neither federal nor state law requires that an employer provide vacation, sick, or personal leave.

finalPay.fired: no state statute sets a deadline (federal law sets none either)
finalPay.quit: no state statute sets a deadline (federal law sets none either)
finalPay.ptoNote: No law requires vacation leave, so payout of unused vacation depends on the employer's policy or contract.

source.quote: The practical alternative is to file a claim for wages against the employer in the small claims court (Magistrate Court) in the county where the employer is located.

ptoSource.quote: Neither federal nor state law requires that an employer provide vacation, sick, or personal leave.

source.quote: Neither the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) nor Georgia law require breaks or meal periods be given to workers.

rightToWorkSource.quote: Georgia is a "Right-to-Work" state. This means that workers may not be required to join a union or make payments to a union as a condition of employment.

notes.text: Georgia's statutory minimum wage is still $5.15 an hour, below the federal $7.25; in practice the federal rate applies to almost all jobs.

source.quote: Georgia's minimum wage is $5.15 per hour, however, with some limited exceptions, the federal minimum wage rate applies.

notes.text: Georgia is both a right-to-work state (no forced union membership or dues) and an at-will state; the state labor department notes that right-to-work only protects against firing for refusing to join a union.

source.quote: This protects a worker who is not hired, or is fired, due to refusal or unwillingness to join a union only.

uncertain: Right-to-work source is the Georgia DOL FAQ, not the statute itself (O.C.G.A. 34-6-20 et seq.); Georgia's code is not hosted on a state site reachable by curl and WebSearch quota was exhausted.
Final pay: no Georgia final-paycheck deadline statute found on official pages; GDOL only points to small claims court. fired/quit left null (believed: no state law).

Georgia 'kin care' law (O.C.G.A. 34-1-10: employers with 25+ employees that offer paid sick leave must allow up to 5 days/year for immediate family care) not verified on an official page, so not included in sickLeave.
localMinWages empty: Georgia preempts local private-sector minimum wages (O.C.G.A. 34-4-3.1) — preemption not verified on an official page; no city private-sector rate exists to our knowledge.
